body.en: Exploratory data analysis uses graphical and numerical summaries to describe the distribution of one variable and relationships between two variables. Always describe shape, centre, spread, and outliers (S-C-S-O).

\[\bar{x}=\frac{\sum x_i}{n}\quad(\text{mean}),\qquad\text{Median }M=\text{middle value of ordered data}.\]

The mean is non-resistant (pulled toward outliers); the median is resistant. Use median when data are skewed.

\[s=\sqrt{\frac{\sum(x_i-\bar{x})^2}{n-1}}\quad(\text{sample SD}),\qquad IQR=Q_3-Q_1.\]

The standard deviation \(s\) measures average distance from the mean. The IQR is resistant. Use IQR (and 5-number summary) with the median; use \(s\) (and \(\bar{x}\)) with symmetric data.

1.5×IQR rule for outliers: a value is an outlier if it is below \(Q_1-1.5\cdot IQR\) or above \(Q_3+1.5\cdot IQR.\)

If \(y_i = a + bx_i\), then:

\[\bar{y}=a+b\bar{x},\quad s_y=|b|\,s_x,\quad M_y=a+b\,M_x.\]

Shape does not change; measures of centre shift by \(a+b\cdot(\text{old})\); spread is multiplied by \(|b|\) (unaffected by \(a\)).

FeatureWhat to report
ShapeSymmetric, skewed left/right, uniform, bimodal
CentreMean or median (state which)
Spread\(s\) or IQR (state which)
OutliersIndividual values; note their direction

For data \((x_i,y_i)\), the least-squares regression line (LSRL) is \(\hat{y}=a+bx\) with

\[b=r\cdot\frac{s_y}{s_x},\quad a=\bar{y}-b\bar{x}.\]

The correlation coefficient \(r\) (\(-1\le r\le1\)) measures strength and direction of linear association. \(r^2\) (coefficient of determination) gives the proportion of variation in \(y\) explained by the linear relationship with \(x.\)

Residual: \(e=y-\hat{y}.\) A residual plot with no pattern confirms a linear model is appropriate.

label.en: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — Exploring Data

body.en:
• Comparative Language on FRQs: When asked to compare two distributions (e.g. two box plots or back-to-back stemplots), you must use comparative adjectives like 'higher', 'more spread out', or 'less skewed'. Simply giving the stats for Distribution A and then Distribution B independently scores an 'Incomplete'.
  • Residual Formula & Interpretation: \( \text{Residual} = y - \hat{y} \) (mnemonic: Actual minus Predicted = AP Stats). A positive residual means the actual point lies above the line (model underestimated); a negative residual means the model overestimated.
  • Interpreting \( r^2 \) (Coefficient of Determination): State: '\( r^2 \% \) of the variation in [response variable in context] is explained by the linear relationship with [explanatory variable in context].' Never say '\( r^2 \) is the chance that the prediction is correct.'
  • Mean vs. Median Under Skewness: When a distribution is skewed right, \( \text{Mean} > \text{Median} \) because extreme high values pull the non-resistant mean upward. When skewed left, \( \text{Mean} < \text{Median} \).

problem.en: Ages: 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 100. Find \(\bar{x}\), \(M\), IQR, and flag outliers.

solution.en:
\(\bar{x}=(12+15+18+21+24+100)/6=190/6\approx31.7.\) \(M=(18+21)/2=19.5.\)

Ordered: 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 100. \(Q_1=15,\;Q_3=24,\;IQR=9.\)

Upper fence: \(24+1.5(9)=37.5.\) The value 100 exceeds 37.5 → outlier. Mean pulled to 31.7; median stays at 19.5 — shows median's resistance.

A regression of price on size gives \(\hat{y}=15000+80x\) (\(r^2=0.81\)). Interpret the slope, \(y\)-intercept, and \(r^2\).

solution.en:
Slope: For each additional square foot, the predicted price increases by $80.

Intercept: A house with 0 sq ft is predicted to cost $15,000 — not meaningful (extrapolation).

\(r^2=0.81\): 81% of the variation in price is explained by the linear relationship with size.

The following data represents test scores (out of 100) for 12 students:
55, 62, 68, 70, 71, 74, 74, 77, 80, 83, 90, 96.

Find the five-number summary and IQR. Identify any potential outliers using the 1.5×IQR rule.

Min=55, Q1=69, Median=75.5, Q3=81.5, Max=96. IQR=12.5.

Fences: lower \(=69-18.75=50.25\), upper \(=81.5+18.75=100.25\). No outliers.

SAT scores are approximately \(N(1060,195^2)\). What proportion of students score above 1400?

\[z=\frac{1400-1060}{195}=\frac{340}{195}\approx1.74.\]

\(P(Z>1.74)=1-0.9591=0.0409\approx4.1\%\) of students score above 1400.

question.en: A dataset has mean 50 and standard deviation 8. (a) What z-score corresponds to a value of 62? (b) What value corresponds to a z-score of −1.5?

A least-squares regression line relates vehicle weight in thousands of pounds (\(x\)) to highway fuel economy in miles per gallon (\(y\)): \(\hat{y} = 48.2 - 6.5x\). A test car weighs 3,200 pounds and achieves an actual fuel economy of 29.5 mpg. (a) Interpret the slope of the regression line in context. (b) Calculate and interpret the residual for this test car.

solution.en:
(a) Slope interpretation: For each additional 1,000 pounds of vehicle weight, the predicted highway fuel economy decreases by 6.5 miles per gallon.

(b) Residual: Here \(x = 3.2\) thousand pounds. Predicted fuel economy: \(\hat{y} = 48.2 - 6.5(3.2) = 48.2 - 20.8 = 27.4\) mpg. The residual is \(e = y - \hat{y} = 29.5 - 27.4 = +2.1\) mpg. The actual fuel economy for this test car is 2.1 mpg higher than predicted by the regression line.

question.en: Parallel box plots display weekly exercise hours for two independent samples of high school athletes and non-athletes. Athletes: Min 4, Q1 8, Med 12, Q3 16, Max 22. Non-athletes: Min 0, Q1 2, Med 4, Q3 7, Max 14. Write a comparative description addressing Center, Unusual points, Shape, and Spread in context.

solution.en:
Center: The median weekly exercise time for athletes (12 hours) is considerably greater than the median for non-athletes (4 hours).

Spread: Athletes show greater variability in exercise hours, with an IQR of \(16 - 8 = 8\) hours compared to an IQR of \(7 - 2 = 5\) hours for non-athletes, and a larger overall range (\(22 - 4 = 18\) vs \(14 - 0 = 14\) hours).

Shape: Both distributions appear roughly symmetric between their quartiles, with whiskers extending similarly on both sides.

Unusual points: Neither group exhibits any outliers under the \(1.5 \times \text{IQR}\) rule (all data points fall within \([Q_1 - 1.5\text{IQR}, Q_3 + 1.5\text{IQR}]\)).
